chapter_theme: Testing the span of life (ஆயுள் பரிட்சை): signs of the body and counts of the breath on its days are said to tell how many years, months or days remain. Around the counts stand verses on the Lord found beyond sound, on watching the failing breath, and on knowing the knower, by which the bond loosens and grace is given.
structure_note: A bodily sign and the sound within (770, 771); watching the breath and its left and right courses (772, 773); a long run of number verses linking breath counts to remaining time (774 to 784); then the Lord who stands beyond karma, the knowledge no one has, and grace (785 to 789).

770.reading: If the hand placed on the head appears straight, the span is six months; if the sign is doubled in excess, it is one month, and a sound is heard daily by the life.
770.nuance: The verse gives a test of the remaining span, but the sign (வைத்தகை சென்னியில் நேரிதாய்), உத்தமம் and மத்தம் can't be fixed; ஓசை (sound) may be an inner sound heard before death.

771.reading: Sound and the Lord are alike in awareness; those who have gone beyond sound contemplate the Lord, and the Lord in their heart is the awareness that has known the sound.
771.nuance: ஓசை is traditionally nada, the inner sound. The variant பிறந்தவர் (those in whom sound arose) reverses 'gone beyond sound' and changes the sense.

772.reading: If one watches the breath that is wasting away, it gives the good of our own dwelling, the teaching that dwells on the flower comes, and one becomes a master in the world.
772.nuance: அழிகின்ற வாயு is the breath spent with each moment. பூமேல் உறைகின்ற போதகம் (the knowledge dwelling on the flower) may be an inner lotus or a god seated on one; போதகம் can also mean an elephant.

773.reading: None master the Lord's left and right; if the left and right turn, it is the woman's; if they keep to their own way, five; if they keep to their own way, a hundred.
773.nuance: இடம் வலம் (left and right) are traditionally the breath in the left and right nostrils, and தலைவன் the breath or the Lord. தையல் (woman) and the numbers five and a hundred (perhaps years) can't be fixed.

774.reading: If the breath runs in the six that has risen, eighty go; reckoned by the seven, it is better; take the two that stand at sixteen, stand clear, and understand this kind.
774.nuance: A count whose scheme I can't recover; ஆறொருபத்து may be sixteen or six and ten.

775.reading: If these eight run to their place, that kind is known as fifty; if the nine stand together, the threefold is thirty-three.
775.nuance: The variants (ஐயொன்பது, ஒன்பது, அன்பது) change the number in line 2, so even the count is unsettled.

776.reading: If three threes and one stand to the end, three eights and four stand as places; if three fives run and stand apart, three and twelve can be seen.
776.nuance: The variant எண்முன்றினாலும் changes the number in line 2. What is counted is not said.

777.reading: If the day-breath runs thirty, the span can be seen; it can be made by putting twelve within; if it is one without refuge it can be sent off; the ten set right can be stored.
777.nuance: பகல் (day) may be the daytime or the right breath, traditionally called the sun. The verbs (see, make, send off, store) suggest the breath can be governed, but the scheme is unclear.

778.reading: If the breath runs properly on two days, the two fours stand without hostility; if the three stand clear to wane, the form can be measured as six.
778.nuance: ஏயிரு and பாயிரு are unclear; the units (days, months, years) are not given.

779.reading: If the four ways of measuring run on that path, one four stands true; if the five that shake run on the pure way, it can be seen in three without stain.
779.nuance: A count whose scheme I can't recover.

780.reading: If the intended ten run, it can be seen; the two mixed can be seen; three fives without mixing can be seen; the one can be seen with the mind fixed.
780.nuance: The refrain காணலுமாகும் (it can be seen) carries the verse. The variant கலப்புற மூவைந்தேழ் reverses 'without mixing' and adds a seven.

781.reading: Considered, in twenty it is six; in twenty-five it is three; in twenty-six it can be shown as two.
781.nuance: Possibly breath counts against remaining days or months. The variants ஈராறு (twelve for six) and ஐந்திற் (five for twenty-five) change the numbers.

782.reading: In twenty-seven it can be shown as one rising mingled; in twenty-eight it can be shown as ten.
782.nuance: The refrain காட்டலுமாகும் (it can be shown) continues 781's series; what is shown is not said.

783.reading: For ten, five, six and eight, the enemy that dreads the burden is ten days; if the weekly course is six and five, it is one day.
783.nuance: The series seems to narrow toward a single remaining day. The variant வகையான்ய் சமாதியில் is garbled but would bring in samadhi.

784.reading: If the joined days become thirty-one, the four become three; if the life goes and the four eights stand together, the measure in the house is two.
784.nuance: மனை (house) and மன்றியல்பு are unclear; மன்று may be the hall where the Lord dances.

785.reading: In the house it is one and three months, Nandi declared it as one in the spring; one who rises beyond karma and opens out into the clear space becomes the Lord who stands joined with himself.
785.nuance: சுனை (spring, pool) may be an inner centre. The second half turns from the counts to the yogi's goal: வினையற (with karma gone) and வெளிச்செய்து (making open, or entering the void).

786.reading: No one knows the fire that measures, no one knows the breath that measures, no one knows the thing that perishes; but I have come to know the knowing.
786.nuance: வன்னி (fire) and வாயு (breath) are the measurers of life the chapter has been counting. அறிவறிந்தேனே can be 'I knew by knowledge' or 'I knew the knower'.

787.reading: Knowing is with the breath and the five senses; if one searches within and keeps world and life from being parted, that knowledge stands dense and shines.
787.nuance: உலகுயிரத்தின் is obscure, taken here as உலகு உயிர் அதன்; பிறிவுசெய்யாவகை (so as not to part) may mean keeping life in the body.

788.reading: That gives grace, and the world is its grace; it graces those of renown in common every day; it gives the honey, the lady of the flower; this is the Lord who grants grace.
788.nuance: அது (that) may be the knowledge of 787 or the Lord. மலர் மங்கையர் செல்வி (the lady among flower-women) is taken as Lakshmi or as Shakti; மது (honey) may be bliss.

789.reading: Nandi, the great one who ordained birth, joined to his sign the fair hut of the body; for those who work so that the bond of the old dwelling, its attachment cut, gives way, understanding widens.
789.nuance: குரம்பை (hut) is a common figure for the body and பழப்பதி (the old town) may be the same body or the round of births. அழப்படி and அகலும் மதியே (the mind, or the moon, widens or departs) are hard.

links.note: Both make the body a temporary dwelling: the Kural's life has only borrowed shelter in it, Tirumular's body is a fair hut the Lord has shaped. The Kural laments the lack of a home; Tirumular looks to loosening the bond of the old dwelling.
741 says people perish without noticing their time run out; 786 names what measures it, fire and breath, and claims the knowledge others lack.

770 reads the span left from a bodily sign and says a sound (ஓசை) comes to the life daily in the last month; 723 counts the senses' signs of the parting day, beginning ஓசையில் ஏழும் (seven in sound). Both treat hearing as a herald of death, and 770 adds the timing in months that 723 leaves unnumbered.

771 says those who have gone beyond sound (ஓசை இறந்தவர்) contemplate the Lord, who is the awareness that knew the sound; 3009 calls the one great god ஓசையும் ஓசை ஒடுக்கமும், both the sound and the subsiding of sound. 3009 explains why going beyond sound in 771 still finds him: he is the stilling as well as the sound.

772 says that watching the breath that is wasting away (அழிகின்ற வாயுவை நோக்கிடில்) brings good and mastery; 786 says no one knows the breath that measures or the thing that perishes (அழிகின்ற அப்பொருள்), yet the speaker has known. Together they name the same perishing breath as what most cannot see and the yogi learns to watch.

773 opens தலைவன் இடம்வலம் சாதிப்பார் இல்லை, none master the left and right; 730 says one who mastered left and right in Shakti's temple (இடம்வலம் சாதித்தான்) hears music at midday and sees Siva. On the plain reading of சாதிப்பார் இல்லை as 'no one', 773 denies the very mastery 730 claims was achieved; if it means only 'few', the two agree.

781 counts இருபதில் ஆறு (six in twenty) and இருபதுடன் ஆறு ... இரண்டு (two at twenty-six); 746 in the previous chapter gives ஆறும் இருபதுக்கு (six for the twenty) and இருபத்தொடு ஆறு with இரண்டு. The same number pairs recur, so the two chapters draw on one counting scheme, which reading them together makes visible even though its units are lost.

782 shows at twenty-seven 'one rising mingled' (இருபத்தேழில் ... கலந்தெழும் ஒன்று); 746 assigns இருபத்தேழு to மதியொன்று, the one moon. Both pair twenty-seven with one, and 746's moon suggests the twenty-seven lunar mansions behind 782's count.

Kural 337 says people do not know whether they will live even one moment (ஒருபொழுதும் வாழ்வது அறியார்); 786 agrees that no one knows the breath that measures life or the thing that perishes (ஆருமறியார்), then adds அறிவறிந்தேனே, 'I have known'. Tirumular grants the Kural's common ignorance but makes the measuring of life knowable to the yogi.

741 says all that is known by the five senses (உற்றறிவு ஐந்தும்), by learning and by mixing them, still does not notice the nazhigai of life being cut away; 787 says knowing is with the breath and the five (வாயுவொடு ஐந்தறிவு), and if one searches within it shines. 787 names the condition, turning the same senses inward with the breath, under which 741's knowing would not be blind.

788 says 'that' gives grace and the world is its grace (அருளானது உலகம்); 1806 says grace is all the elemental world (அருளே சகலமும் ஆய பவுதிகம்) and the moving and unmoving. Both identify the world itself with grace rather than with what grace saves one from.

source_issues: 773: line 4 reads தலைவ நிடம், a misprint for தலைவ னிடம்.
775: variants (ஐயொன்பது, ஒன்பது, அன்பது) change the number in line 2.
776: the variant எண்முன்றினாலும் changes the number in line 2.
781: variants ஈராறாகும் and ஐந்திற் change the numbers.
783: the variant வகையான்ய் சமாதியில் is garbled.
787: உலகுயி ரத்தின் is obscure and may be corrupt.
